added_models.model: Human anti-GM-CSF-autoantibody pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (acquired loss of GM-CSF signalling)

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 10499925, PMC2195627). model_kind human_genetic is the nearest enum: the state is an acquired autoimmune loss of GM-CSF signalling, not a germline genotype. Uchida 2004 (10.1182/blood-2003-05-1565) showed the autoantibody neutralises lung GM-CSF 4000-58,000-fold in excess; Uchida 2009 (10.1182/blood-2008-05-155689; PubMed lists the DOI as blood-2009-05-155689, which redirects to it) defined the critical autoantibody threshold for PAP.
safety.model: Human anti-GM-CSF-autoantibody pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (acquired loss of GM-CSF signalling)
safety.quote: We report here that I-PAP is an autoimmune disease with neutralizing antibody of immunoglobulin G isotype against granulocyte/macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF).
safety.note: Neutralising anti-GM-CSF autoantibodies in every idiopathic PAP patient: people, not mice, show what sustained GM-CSF neutralisation does to the lung.
safety.short: Human autoantibody PAP predicts lung harm
safety.judgement: Own track from the GM-CSF-null mouse: a different system (acquired antibody neutralisation in people) with a different prediction (PAP only above a neutralising threshold, Uchida 2009), and the one the RA trials cited when they chose SP-D, KL-6 and PFT monitoring (Behrens 2015 ref 21; NEXUS ref 32).

safety.magnitude_basis: serum SP-D and PFTs unchanged after four weekly IV doses of 0.3-1.5 mg/kg MOR103 (69 treated) against the model's threshold-conditional PAP prediction; depth of alveolar GM-CSF neutralisation not measured
safety.confidence_note: OA full text (PMC4431325; online 2014-02-17, registry NCT01023256 results first posted 2014-05-08). Four weeks of partial neutralisation cannot produce PAP on the model's own terms, so this first dataset tests only the conditional arm; no trial measured whether pharmacological neutralisation crossed the Uchida 2009 threshold (no BAL GM-CSF bioactivity).
safety.model: Human anti-GM-CSF-autoantibody pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (acquired loss of GM-CSF signalling)
safety.quote: Surfactant D levels remained normal and there was no overall pattern of PFT alterations in MOR103-treated subjects.
safety.note: MOR103 Phase 1b/2a: SP-D and PFTs monitored because of autoantibody PAP; both normal after four weekly doses, as the threshold model predicts.
safety.short: No PAP surrogate rise, as predicted
safety.judgement: same, not contra: the human model predicts PAP only after prolonged, complete neutralisation above a critical autoantibody threshold (Uchida 2004, 2009), and the sponsor stated the same reading ('clinical onset of PAP requires prolonged and complete inhibition of GMCSF', contRAst 3 protocol, citing hereditary CSF2RA PAP). Normal SP-D and PFTs at partial four-week neutralisation agree with that prediction in direction, where the knockout's unconditional prediction is scored contra. comparison_stated true because Behrens names the autoantibody-PAP association as the reason for the readouts and reports them. Hinge for the adjudicator (rule question 5): if a conditional prediction is unscorable without measuring the condition this falls to untested; it turns contra only if neutralisation is shown to have crossed the threshold.

safety.magnitude_basis: CEA, KL-6 and SP-D without treatment trend over 12 weeks of namilumab 20-150 mg SC (81 treated); neutralisation depth unmeasured
safety.confidence_note: OA full text (PMC6471864). NEXUS monitored lungs 'because of the theoretical risk of developing pulmonary alveolar proteinosis when using therapeutic antibodies that target GM-CSF', citing the Japanese autoimmune-PAP cohort (Inoue 2008, 10.1164/rccm.200708-1271OC), so the human analogue is the stated model. Year follows the registry results posting (NCT02379091, 2018-09-14), as the draft dates this trial; the quotable sentence is in the 2019 paper.
safety.model: Human anti-GM-CSF-autoantibody pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (acquired loss of GM-CSF signalling)
safety.quote: With regard to change from baseline in biomarkers with the potential for early detection of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (carcinoembryonic antigen, KL-6, and SP-D), there were no trends associated with namilumab treatment.
safety.note: NEXUS: no trend in CEA, KL-6 or SP-D over 12 weeks of namilumab; AEs suggestive of PAP adjudicated as other diagnoses.
safety.short: No PAP biomarker trend, second drug
safety.judgement: Second member drug, three times the exposure, same direction; still partial neutralisation, so it strengthens the conditional-arm agreement rather than testing the threshold.

safety.magnitude_basis: zero PAP in 2915 patients on weekly 90/150 mg otilimab for 7-896 days; neutralisation depth unmeasured
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 40044198, PMC11883618). Registry NCT04333147 results posted 2024-02-07 carry AE tables but no quotable PAP sentence, so the paper dates the entry, as on the knockout track. Weekly dosing held CCL17 engagement, yet no trial measured alveolar GM-CSF bioactivity; the model's threshold remains the unmeasured condition.
safety.model: Human anti-GM-CSF-autoantibody pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (acquired loss of GM-CSF signalling)
safety.quote: There were no instances of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP), active tuberculosis (TB), TB reactivation or serious hypersensitivity reactions.
safety.note: contRAst X: no PAP in 2915 patients over up to 2.5 years at the weekly regimen that sustained engagement.
safety.reason: No PAP below the neutralising threshold
safety.judgement: Largest exposure; the knockout scores this contra, the human model same, because its prediction is conditional on complete neutralisation that pharmacological dosing was not shown to reach. If a later source shows alveolar GM-CSF bioactivity was abolished at 150 mg weekly, this track turns contra.

added_models.model: Cynomolgus monkey 13-week SC and 26-week IV GLP toxicology of otilimab (GSK3196165)

dose.confidence_note: Protocol Amendment 02 (approved 2020-01-21), uploaded to ClinicalTrials.gov 2023-01-31; a registry-hosted document, scored tier 3. The GLP studies are unpublished and predate the protocol (the 26-week study had to precede BAROQUE's 50-week dosing), so 2020 is the earliest public date, not the first use. NOEL 5 mg/kg; dose levels and exposures sit in the Investigator Brochure, which is not public.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey 13-week SC and 26-week IV GLP toxicology of otilimab (GSK3196165)
dose.quote: The highest dose of 150 mg weekly provides a 3 to 5-fold safety margin to the 5 mg/kg dose in the 26-week monkey toxicology study where no foamy alveolar macrophages were observed (NOEL).
dose.note: Sponsor's dose rationale: 150 mg weekly sits 3-5-fold below the 26-week monkey NOEL for foamy alveolar macrophages.
dose.short: Monkey NOEL margin stated for 150 mg
dose.judgement: Own track: a different system (the product itself in a primate, GLP toxicology) making a different prediction (a tolerability margin for the clinical dose) from the arthritis mice (efficacy exposure) and the knockout (unconditional PAP). Decision 16 scores this toxic end of the window; the efficacy end stays on the 22E9 track.

dose.magnitude_basis: 150 mg weekly, the dose at the stated 3-5-fold margin, given for up to 24 weeks in contRAst 3 (549 treated across arms) with adverse-event incidence matching placebo and sarilumab; human exposures not reported in the paper
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 37696589, PMC10646837; registry NCT04134728 results 2023-07-17). The efficacy end of the dose rule (150 mg weekly missed ACR20 here) is scored on the 22E9 track; this entry scores only the tolerability margin (decision 16).
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey 13-week SC and 26-week IV GLP toxicology of otilimab (GSK3196165)
dose.quote: The incidence of adverse or serious adverse events was similar across treatment groups.
dose.note: contRAst 3 dosed 150 mg weekly, the dose the monkey margin covered, with adverse-event rates matching placebo and sarilumab.
dose.short: Stated margin held at 150 mg weekly
dose.judgement: Decision 16: the model stated the clinical dose was tolerated (NOEL margin) and patients were dosed to it without the lung toxicity, so dose is same with margin_stated. contRAst 1 and 2 (registry results 2023-10-25 and 2023-11-30) dosed the same regimen; contRAst 3 is the earliest public record.

dose.magnitude_basis: zero PAP and no lung finding of the monkey type reported in 2915 patients at 90/150 mg weekly for up to 896 days
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 40044198, PMC11883618; registry NCT04333147 results 2024-02-07, no quotable sentence there). The extension was cut short by the programme decision, so the margin was tested to 2.5 years, not lifelong.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey 13-week SC and 26-week IV GLP toxicology of otilimab (GSK3196165)
dose.quote: There were no instances of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP), active tuberculosis (TB), TB reactivation or serious hypersensitivity reactions.
dose.note: contRAst X: no PAP over up to 2.5 years at the covered dose; the monkey margin held to the end of the programme.
dose.reason: Monkey NOEL margin held in patients
dose.judgement: Strengthens the 2023 call with the direct lung readout at 13x the exposure; the harm is still counted once, here in dose, per decision 16.

safety.confidence_note: Protocol Amendment 02 (approved 2020-01-21, uploaded 2023-01-31), risk table pp. 20-21; the sentence runs across a page break in the PDF. Dose levels with and without the finding are said to exist but are given only in the Investigator Brochure.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 13-week SC and 26-week IV GLP toxicology of otilimab (GSK3196165)
safety.quote: Non-adverse minimal to mild foamy alveolar macrophage accumulation were noted in lungs of monkeys in the 13-week SC and 26-week IV toxicology studies but were reversible following an off drug period.
safety.note: Otilimab itself gave monkeys reversible foamy alveolar macrophages, the PAP precursor, above a dose level; the margin is scored in dose.
safety.judgement: Untested rather than same: the species predicted the on-target lung change only above the NOEL, patients were never exposed there, and decision 16 counts the harm once, in the dose cell where the margin held. The prediction itself (foamy macrophages at supra-NOEL exposure) has no patient comparison.

considered_not_added: GSK press release 2022-10-27 (contRAst programme update): a dating lead on the existing 22E9 efficacy/dose track, not a model system; left to the adjudicator's corrections of efficacy 4 / dose 3

Behrens 2015 and NEXUS (Taylor 2019) as earlier datasets on the GM-CSF-null knockout track (mouse-gmcsf-null-pap): existing track, dating only; used here only as the patient side of the new human-autoantibody track

Lenzilumab LIVE-AIR (Temesgen 2022, 10.1016/S2213-2600(21)00494-X) and namilumab CATALYST (Fisher 2022, 10.1016/S2213-2600(21)00460-4): importable COVID-19 safety datasets for the existing knockout track (strengthens only, imported_from MONDO:0100096); a single short course cannot test PAP on the human model's own terms, so not added to the new track either
Mavrilimumab synovial-explant SCID model and its cynomolgus toxicology (foamy alveolar macrophages): receptor antibody, out of class; member list not widened
TJ003234 (plonmarlimab) cynomolgus GLP toxicology (NOAEL 60 mg/kg; one monkey with minimal alveolar protein): non-member anti-GM-CSF antibody, out of class

Sakagami 2009/2010 non-human-primate passive transfer of PAP-patient autoantibodies (NEJM 361:2679; AJRCCM 2010): reproduces PAP but was never compared with anti-GM-CSF trial patients; a retrodiction of the disease, not of the class

Hereditary PAP from CSF2RA/CSF2RB mutations (Suzuki 2008, Martinez-Moczygemba 2008): the contRAst protocol cites them, with the autoantibody literature, for one premise (PAP needs prolonged, complete inhibition); same prediction family as the autoantibody track and no trial monitored on it separately, so folded into that track's note rather than a fourth human track

Sponsor DAS28-CRP exposure-response model used to pick 90/150 mg weekly (contRAst protocol: '150 mg is predicted to provide greater clinical benefit'): fitted to BAROQUE patient data, structure and parameters unpublished, so not a preclinical system and no model source beyond one protocol paragraph; flagged for the adjudicator as a possible in_silico track if sponsor dose-selection models are wanted

Ex-vivo human whole-blood / monocyte GM-CSF neutralisation assays used as clinical PD readouts: clinical assays on dosed patients, not a model system with a prediction to compare; no source pairing one with trial outcome found
Mouse PK/PD model (Koch 2012): already the model_src of the 22E9 dose track; same system
